Welcome Wednesday – Every Week at 10am! Prospective parents are warmly invited to join us for a guided tour of our school and meet our Senior Leadership Team. Discover our learning environment, ask questions and see what makes our school community the place where 'Every child is a success'
Welcome to Mulgrave Primary School
It is with great pleasure that we welcome you to our school website — a window into the vibrant, inclusive, and diverse community that makes Mulgrave Primary School the place where children thrive.
At Mulgrave, we live by the motto Learn | Believe | Succeed — a powerful message created by our Junior Leadership Team that lies at the heart of everything we do. We believe that we are curious when we learn, brave when we believe and proud when we succeed.
Every child at Mulgrave is nurtured to grow in confidence, curiosity, and compassion. This is underpinned by academic excellence and high expectations, ensuring that education is not only about achievement but also about developing kind, thoughtful, and resilient individuals who are proud of who they are and excited about who they can become.
If you're exploring options for your child’s education, we warmly invite you to discover what makes Mulgrave such a unique and inspiring place to learn and grow. Our website offers just a glimpse into the rich learning experiences, meaningful achievements, and nurturing environment that define our school but nothing compares to seeing it in action.
We look forward to welcoming you soon.
Mrs Weaver Headteacher
Book a visit to Mulgrave Primary School
Why Choose Mulgrave Primary School?
There are so many reasons to join Mulgrave Primary School! We’re proud of the warm, inclusive community we’ve built and the opportunities we provide for every child to thrive.
Below, you’ll find key information about the things that make Mulgrave great — from our dedicated staff and inspiring curriculum to the values that shape our school every day. We also offer a vast Forest School overlooking Mulgrave Lake, giving children the chance to learn and explore in nature, and a welcoming Nursery for 2‑year‑olds to help our youngest learners get the very best start.
But don’t just take our word for it — Use the quick links below to explore more about us, including what our families say, our values, and the opportunities that make Mulgrave such a special place for every child.
Below you will find instructions on how to add calendars from different platforms:
At Mulgrave, we believe every school day counts. Coming to school regularly and on time is essential to help children Learn, Believe and Succeed — academically, socially, and emotionally.
Why Good Attendance Matters
Attending school every day helps children: Achieve academic success – Good attendance means children can keep up with learning, understand lessons better, and make strong progress in all subjects.Build friendships and confidence – Regular school attendance helps children stay connected with their classmates, develop key social skills, and feel a sense of belonging. Secure a brighter future – Good habits start early. Strong attendance in primary school sets children up for success in secondary school, future careers, and beyond.

British Values at Mulgrave Primary School
At Mulgrave Primary School, we are proud to actively promote the fundamental British values of democracy, the rule of law, individual liberty, mutual respect, and tolerance of those with different faiths and beliefs. These values are woven into our curriculum, our ethos, and our daily practice—supporting every child to learn, believe, and succeed.
We recognise our responsibility to nurture pupils’ spiritual, moral, social, and cultural development as part of a broad and balanced education. Our commitment to British values is not just about meeting statutory expectations—it’s about preparing children to thrive as thoughtful, respectful citizens in modern Britain and beyond.
We also embed the principles of the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child (UNCRC) across school life, ensuring that children’s rights are understood, respected, and upheld. These values are universal, shared across many cultures and communities, and help us build a school where every child is seen, celebrated, and empowered to succeed. We are working towards our ‘Rights Respecting School Award’.
Celebrating Our Place in Britain
At Mulgrave, we celebrate the rich diversity of our school community and the heritage of the area we serve. We encourage children to take pride in where they live, to understand their local history, and to explore how it connects to the wider national story. Through our curriculum, children learn about:
Britain’s capital cities, counties, rivers and mountains
How We Promote British Values
We promote freedom of choice and the right to express beliefs respectfully. Within a safe and supportive environment, children are encouraged to:
Mutual Respect and Tolerance
Respect is a cornerstone of our school culture and our first school rule. We celebrate the many faiths, cultures, and backgrounds represented in our community, and teach children to value difference. This is reflected in:
Children learn that their actions affect others, and that kindness and respect are essential to building a fair and inclusive society.
From the earliest years, children learn about rules, fairness, and responsibility. We reinforce this through:
Children understand that laws protect everyone and that they have a role in upholding them.
At Mulgrave, British values are not just taught—they are lived. They underpin our vision of “Every Child a Success” and help us create a school where every learner is prepared to contribute positively to society, now and in the future.

pageCache.text:
Our Vision
‘Every Child a success’
At Mulgrave Primary School, ‘Every Child a Success’ is more than our vision—it’s the guiding principle that shapes our ethos and drives everything we do. We believe in building strong foundations in learning that will support every child well beyond their time at Mulgrave.
Our school motto Learn, Believe, Succeed reflects the values we instil in our children every day. We believe that we are curious when we learn, brave when we believe, and proud when we succeed. These values are the cornerstones of our approach to education and personal development.
We are proud to be a richly diverse and inclusive community where children are encouraged to explore their passions, grow in confidence, and feel a deep sense of belonging. At the heart of this is a strong focus on academic excellence. We aim to ensure that every child leaves Year 6 with secure foundations in reading, writing and maths, and is ready to take on the next stage of their learning with confidence and curiosity.
Our role is to nurture not just academic achievement, but the whole child—helping them to thrive in a safe, positive, and values-led environment where learning is meaningful, progress is celebrated, and every child is equipped to succeed.
At Mulgrave Primary School, we believe every child deserves to be seen, celebrated, and equipped to succeed—academically, socially, and personally. Rooted in our ethos of Every Child a Success and our guiding motto Learn, Believe, Succeed, we are proud to be a nurturing, inclusive, and aspirational learning community in the heart of Woolwich.

pageCache.pageTitle: Welcome to Nursery | Mulgrave Primary School
pageCache.text:
Welcome to Nursery
At Mulgrave Primary School, our nursery is a joyful, nurturing space where every child is seen, celebrated, and supported to thrive. We believe that the early years are the foundation for lifelong learning—and we’re passionate about giving every child the best possible start.
Our nursery is more than just a place to learn—it’s a place to belong. We work in close partnership with families to create a warm, inclusive environment where children feel safe, curious, and confident. Through play, exploration, and meaningful relationships, we support each child’s holistic development—emotionally, socially, physically, and academically.
Guided by our ethos of Learn, Believe, Succeed, we tailor our provision to meet the needs of every learner. Whether they’re building friendships, discovering minibeasts in our Forest School, or taking their first steps into phonics, our children are encouraged to ask questions, take risks, and grow in independence.
At Mulgrave Nursery, we believe in the power of early education to shape futures. Every moment matters—and every child is a success.

Book a visit to Mulgrave Primary School
About Us
At Mulgrave Primary School, we believe every child deserves to be seen, celebrated, and equipped to succeed—academically, socially, and personally. Rooted in our ethos of Every Child a Success and our guiding motto Learn, Believe, Succeed, we are proud to be a nurturing, inclusive, and aspirational learning community in the heart of Woolwich.
Who We Are
Mulgrave is more than a school—it’s a family. Led by a visionary team of educators and supported by a vibrant network of parents, carers, and governors, we work together to create a safe, inspiring environment where children thrive. Our curriculum is rich, inclusive, and ambitious, designed to spark curiosity, build resilience, and lay strong foundations for lifelong learning.
Our Values
Our five core values are woven into every aspect of school life. They guide our behaviour, shape our culture, and empower every learner to grow not just in knowledge, but in character.
What We Offer
Our Vision
We are on a journey to excellence, guided by our strategic priorities and aligned with the latest Ofsted framework. Whether refining our staff handbook, embedding our values into daily routines, or shaping our School Development Plan, we are relentless in our pursuit of clarity, consistency, and impact.
At Mulgrave, we don’t just teach—we inspire. We don’t just care—we champion. And we don’t just prepare children for the next stage—we equip them to learn, believe, and succeed in every stage of life.

Welcome
It is with great pleasure that we welcome you to our school website—a window into the vibrant, inclusive, and diverse community that makes Mulgrave Primary School so special.
At Mulgrave, we live by the motto Learn. Believe. Succeed.—a powerful message created by our Junior Leadership Team that lies at the heart of everything we do. We believe that we are curious when we learn, brave when we believe, and proud when we succeed.
Every child at Mulgrave is nurtured to grow in confidence, curiosity, and compassion. We see education as more than academic achievement—it’s about developing kind, thoughtful, and resilient individuals who are proud of who they are and excited about who they can become.
If you're exploring options for your child’s education, we warmly invite you to discover what makes Mulgrave such a unique and inspiring place to learn and grow. Our website offers just a glimpse into the rich learning experiences, meaningful achievements, and nurturing environment that define our school—but nothing compares to seeing it in action.
We look forward to welcoming you soon.
Warm regards, Mrs Weaver Headteacher

Working Together: Parent Partnership in Nursery
At Mulgrave Primary School, we believe that strong parent partnerships are the foundation of successful early learning. Parents are a child’s first and most important teacher—and when home and school work together in harmony, children flourish.
In our nursery, we place great value on building open, honest, and collaborative relationships with families. We know that when parents feel informed, involved, and respected, children feel secure, confident, and ready to learn. That’s why we make time to listen, share, and celebrate every child’s journey—together.
From settling-in conversations and daily updates to parent workshops and stay-and-play sessions, we actively encourage families to be part of nursery life. We welcome your insights, questions, and contributions, and we’re committed to working with you every step of the way.
Our shared goal is simple: Every Child a Success. By nurturing strong home-school connections, we help every child learn, believe, and succeed—starting with the very first steps of their educational journey.

pageCache.pageTitle: Home - Start Greenwich | Mulgrave Primary School
pageCache.text:
Home-Start Greenwich
Partnering with Home-Start Greenwich
Mulgrave Primary School is proud to host Home-Start Greenwich within our school. We’re excited to strengthen the connection between our school and Home-Start, working together to give children and families in our community the very best start in life.
Home-Start Greenwich is an independent charity, affiliated with Home-Start UK, that has been supporting families with young children across the Royal Borough of Greenwich for over 25 years. At the heart of their work is a dedicated home-visiting volunteer service, where trained volunteers offer one-to-one weekly support to families in their own homes—because they believe, like us, that parenting begins at home.
In addition to home-based support, Home-Start Greenwich runs two Ofsted-registered nursery settings in Plumstead, offering a total of 96 places for children aged 0 to 5. Their work is further extended through close partnership with Royal Greenwich, delivering a range of children’s centre services across seven community sites.
We are proud to work alongside an organisation that shares our commitment to supporting families and empowering every child to learn, believe, and succeed—reflecting our shared vision to make Every Child a Success.

pageCache.pageTitle: Unicef Rights Respecting School  | Mulgrave Primary School
pageCache.text:
Rights Respecting Schools
At Mulgrave Primary School, we are proud to be working towards the UNICEF Rights Respecting Schools Award (RRSA). This recognises our commitment to placing children's rights at the heart of everything we do. Guided by the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child (UNCRC), we are creating a school where every child feels safe, respected, valued and empowered to achieve their full potential. Our Rights Respecting journey supports our vision that every child can be successful in their own right and helps to ensure that every member of our school community is treated with dignity, fairness and respect.
Children's rights are woven throughout our curriculum, teaching and learning, helping pupils to develop the knowledge, skills and values they need to become confident, compassionate and responsible citizens. We encourage our pupils to understand not only their own rights but also the responsibilities that come with respecting the rights of others. Through meaningful pupil voice, collaborative learning and opportunities such as our Active Rights Ambassadors, children are empowered to share their ideas, influence positive change and play an active role in shaping our school community.
Our Rights Respecting ethos underpins our approach to behaviour, relationships and wellbeing. By promoting kindness, inclusion, equality and mutual respect, we foster a positive learning environment where every child feels they belong and can thrive. As we continue our journey towards becoming a Rights Respecting School, we are strengthening our commitment to developing respectful relationships, celebrating diversity and ensuring that the voice of every child is heard, valued and acted upon. Together, we are building a school community where rights are lived every day and every child is encouraged to flourish.

Governors
Chair of Governors- Chris Tuffey
I am honoured to be Chair of Governors at Mulgrave School, having joined as a co-opted Governor in early 2022. As a school governor since 2008, my motivation stems from a deep belief in the transformative power of education and its pivotal role in shaping a safe, happy, and successful future for our children.
Mulgrave stands out to me as an energetic school that has created a safe and stimulating environment, serving as a launchpad for children to realise their full potential. The school fosters a lifelong love of learning, providing students with the tools they need to navigate the world ahead successfully.
With nearly 40 years in financial services, including international experience, I believe I bring a wealth of insights to the governing board. I strongly advocate for the importance of numeracy and confidence with numbers, recognising their role in social and economic mobility. I have witnessed firsthand the value that a diverse and inclusive culture brings, and I am passionate about fostering such an environment at Mulgrave.
Beyond academics, I have a keen interest in sports, health, and overall wellness, understanding the positive impact of physical activity on the mind. I believe in nurturing not only academic excellence but also the holistic well-being of our students.
It is a privilege to contribute to a school that is known for its nurturing, creative, and successful approach to education. I am excited about the opportunity to be part of Mulgrave's journey in providing an enriching educational experience for your children.
Annual Governance Statement
The Governing Board of Mulgrave Primary School

pageCache.pageTitle: Parents guide to EHCPs | Mulgrave Primary School
pageCache.text:
Parents guide to EHCPs
Understanding Education, Health and Care Plans (EHCPs)
At Mulgrave Primary School, we are committed to ensuring that every child is a success. For children with Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND), an Education, Health and Care Plan (EHCP) can provide the tailored support they need to thrive.
What is an EHCP?
An EHCP is a legal document for children and young people aged 0 to 25 who require extra support beyond what is ordinarily available in schools or colleges. It outlines:
The child’s or young person’s education, health, and care needs
The additional support required to meet those needs
The outcomes the child or young person wants to achieve
This plan is developed in partnership with parents, schools, and relevant professionals to ensure a holistic approach to the child's development.
Why is an EHCP Important?
An EHCP is crucial because it:
Provides a clear, coordinated approach to meeting a child’s needs across education, health, and care services.
Ensures the child receives appropriate support tailored to their individual requirements.
Facilitates regular reviews to adapt the support as the child grows and their needs evolve.
Empowers families by involving them in the planning and decision-making process.
How to Apply for an EHCP
In the first instance, please speak to your child’s class teacher. They may suggest arranging a meeting with Mr. Black, our SENCO, to discuss your child’s needs.
The school can apply for an EHCP on your behalf, or you can choose to make a parental request yourself.
Most children will have already received SEND support within school or nursery before an EHCP is considered. If this support has not led to sufficient progress, an EHCP may be the next step.
To request an EHCP via a parental request, the following steps are involved
If you need support or guidance at any stage, please contact Mr. Black, our SENCO, who is here to help you through the process.
What Does an EHCP Entitle My Child To?
An EHCP entitles your child to:
Personalised support tailored to their specific needs.
Access to appropriate educational settings that can meet their needs.
Regular reviews to ensure the support remains effective and relevant.
Involvement in the decision-making process, ensuring the child's voice is heard.
How Mulgrave Supports the EHCP Process
At Mulgrave, our Special Educational Needs Coordinator (SENCo), Mr. Black, plays a pivotal role in supporting families through the EHCP process. He works closely with parents, teachers, and external professionals to:
Assess and identify your child's needs.
Coordinate the development of the EHCP.
Monitor the implementation of the plan to ensure effective support.
If you have questions or need assistance regarding EHCPs, please contact Mr. Black through the school office. He is here to guide and support you every step of the way.

pageCache.pageTitle: Forest School & Outdoor Learning | Mulgrave Primary School
pageCache.text:
Outdoor Learning & Forest School at Mulgrave
At Mulgrave Primary School, we believe that nature is one of the most powerful teachers. Our extensive outdoor grounds—including a large, dedicated Forest School space overlooking a tranquil lake—offer children the chance to immerse themselves in the natural world, sparking curiosity, creativity, and confidence.
Outdoor learning is central to our ethos of Every Child a Success. It supports holistic development—nurturing children’s physical health, emotional wellbeing, social skills, and academic growth. Whether they’re climbing, building, exploring, or simply sitting quietly by the water, children learn to take risks, solve problems, and connect deeply with the world around them.
Our Forest School is a rich, living classroom filled with trees, logs, rocks, and wildlife. It’s a place where children can dig, discover, and delight in the changing seasons. Overlooking the lake, the space invites calm reflection as well as energetic exploration—helping children regulate emotions, build resilience, and develop a lifelong respect for the environment.
Forest School is more than just outdoor play. It’s an evidence-based approach to learning that fosters independence, teamwork, and self-esteem through hands-on experiences in nature. Sessions are led by trained staff and tailored to each age group—from nursery children searching for minibeasts to Year 6 pupils learning fire safety and bushcraft skills.
At Mulgrave, outdoor learning isn’t a treat—it’s a right. We ensure that every child has regular access to our Forest School, because we know that when children feel free, grounded, and inspired, they truly learn, believe, and succeed.

pageCache.pageTitle: Travel for Life Gold Accreditation | Mulgrave Primary School
pageCache.text:
Travel for Life Gold Accreditation
Active Travel at Mulgrave Primary School
At Mulgrave, we are passionate about encouraging our pupils and families to choose active travel — walking, cycling or scooting — as their way of getting to and from school. Not only is this a healthier option, but it also helps reduce congestion and pollution around our school.
We’re proud to say that over 70% of our children now walk, cycle or scoot to school regularly, and we’re working hard to increase that number even more. Fewer car journeys mean cleaner air and a safer environment for everyone.
As part of our commitment to sustainable travel, our pupils have taken part in exciting learning activities across the school, exploring:
The impact of air quality on our health
How physical activity supports learning and boosts brain power
Road safety skills, including the Green Cross Code
Thanks to the enthusiasm of our children and staff — and a lot of hard work — we were thrilled to achieve Gold accreditation from Travel for Life (formerly STARS) in September 2024!
To keep the momentum going, we have a brilliant team of Travel for Life Ambassadors (formerly JTAs) who work closely with Ms Catargiu. They lead assemblies, run competitions, and organise challenges to promote safe, clean, and active travel across our school community.
Active travel is an important part of our wider commitment to health, wellbeing, and looking after our planet. Thank you for supporting us on this journey — one step, scoot or pedal at a time!

pageCache.pageTitle: Open Days and Coffee Mornings | Mulgrave Primary School
pageCache.text:
Open Days and Coffee Mornings
We’re delighted to invite families to come and see what makes Mulgrave Primary School such a special place. Our upcoming Open Day is the perfect opportunity to explore our school, meet our staff, and discover how we support every child to thrive. We welcome families looking for places not only in Reception but across other year groups too—please contact our school office for the latest information on available spaces.
Mulgrave families are also warmly encouraged to join us for our Coffee Mornings, advertised through our parents’ mail. These free sessions are a wonderful chance to meet new families, catch up with friends, and become part of our wider school community. Alongside our friendly gatherings, we host focused coffee mornings with specialists from agencies we work closely with—such as Speech and Language Therapists and Autism Outreach teams—providing valuable insights and support for families.
Whether you’re visiting us for the first time or already part of our Mulgrave family, we look forward to welcoming you. Come along, stay for a coffee, and connect in a supportive, friendly environment where every family belongs.

Curriculum & Learning
At Mulgrave Primary School, we recognise that the foundations laid in the early years are critical to a child’s lifelong learning journey. Early development shapes not only academic success but also emotional resilience, social confidence, and a love of discovery. That is why our curriculum is carefully designed to nurture curiosity, creativity, and independence from the very beginning, ensuring that every child has the best possible start.
We take a holistic approach to education, understanding that children thrive when their intellectual, physical, emotional, and social needs are met in harmony. Our teaching goes beyond the classroom, embedding values of respect, kindness, and perseverance into daily learning. By creating a safe, stimulating environment, we encourage children to explore, question, and grow—developing both the skills and the character needed to flourish in an ever-changing world.
Crucially, we believe that education is a shared journey between school and home. We actively work with families to support the early development of their children, building strong partnerships that reinforce learning and wellbeing. Through open communication, workshops, and collaborative activities, we empower parents and carers to be part of their child’s growth. Together, we ensure that every Mulgrave learner is not only prepared for the next stage of education, but for life: ready to learn, believe, and succeed.
